ev.q: Antigen test results and associated individual characteristics were analyzed among 3,502 infections
54% of persons had positive SARS-CoV-2 antigen test results.
396 of 729 persons evaluated (54.3%) had a positive antigen test result
Overall, 396 (54.3%) tested persons had a positive BinaxNOW antigen test
A positive antigen test was more likely after a symptomatic infection (361 of 564, 64.0%) than after an asymptomatic infection (35 of 165, 21.2%)
In multivariable models, a positive antigen test result was more likely after 5 days than after 9 days
data were cross-sectional rather than longitudinal.
The proportion of positive antigen test results declined with the number of days since an initial positive test

methods_quotes.q: Multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify factors independently associated with a positive follow-up antigen test result
using a two-sided significance threshold of p<0.05; univariate comparisons were made using the chi-square test.
Adjusted for age group, days since symptom onset or positive test result, previous infection status, previous vaccination status, and whether symptoms were reported.
